---
title: "Rolling Hash: Turn a String into Arithmetic"
description: "A mathematical interview pattern explained by a small example and proof."
---

## Recognition trigger

Fast substring equality candidates, repetitive strings and pattern matching.

## Main question

**How can two strings be compared through a compact algebraic fingerprint?**

## Formula worth memorising

$$
H(s)=\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}c_i p^i\right)\bmod m
$$

**Every symbol explained:** s is a string of length n; c_i is integer code assigned to character at position i; p is a chosen polynomial base; m is a positive modulus; Σ adds powers of p weighted by character codes; H is the resulting residue.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For codes a=1,b=2 and base p=3, modulus m=101, H('ab')=1×3⁰+2×3¹=1+6=7. H('ba')=2×1+1×3=5, so these strings are distinguishable by this hash.

## Derivation and correctness reasoning

A polynomial representation permits updating substring hashes using arithmetic on powers of p, rather than scanning all characters for every comparison. Prefix-hash variants enable fast substring-hash queries after preprocessing.

## Failure modes and assumptions

Distinct strings can collide modulo m, so hash equality does not prove string equality. For security-sensitive or exact problems, confirm candidates directly or use collision-free methods; randomisation and double hashing only reduce collision likelihood.

## The 20-second memory card

**Memorise: Encode characters as polynomial coefficients, take a modulus, and remember collisions prevent deterministic equality proofs.**

Practise reciting the invariant or proof, not merely the equation.

**Interview problems:** Repeated DNA Sequences; Longest Duplicate Substring.
